A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LCoW research. Text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C are readable and can be matched across versions; the pagination differences do not indicate missing material.

before.justification: v1 reports original WebShop, WorkArena, and WebArena experiments, including benchmark results in Tables 1-2 and qualitative and generalization analyses in Appendices A-B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark experiments and appendix analyses, including numerical success rates, rewards, and agent rollout comparisons.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same contextualization module, successful-trajectory collection, candidate sampling and retry procedure, multi-agent action-matching reward, and supervised updates.

E1.justification: Both versions use WebShop, WorkArena, and WebArena, including the same unseen-task-type, unseen-category, and held-out-website evaluations in Section 4.3 and Appendix B.

E2.justification: The raw-observation, self-contextualization, and behavior-cloning comparisons are unchanged. Figure 5 retains the same WebN-T5, ASH, ReAct, WebGUM, LASER, and AgentQ baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix B retain identical splits, evaluation metrics, training settings, and generalization partitions. These include 500 WebShop evaluation tasks and 165 evaluation tasks each for WorkArena and WebArena.

E4.justification: The contextualization examples, rollout comparisons, action-step distributions, training-iteration analysis, and generalization tests in Section 4.3 and Appendices A-B are retained without added or removed analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports additional repeated runs, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Figure 14 retains the same task-wise distributions of action counts.

E6.justification: All matched numerical and qualitative results are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains Gemini-1.5-flash with LCoW at 62.8% success and 0.803 reward, while Table 3 retains 0.0% unseen-category success for both evaluated agents.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation in Section 2, contextualization and action equations in Section 3.1, and training mathematics in Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Neither version adds theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about separating web understanding from decision making, improving agents across model scales, generalizing to unseen agents, and exceeding human-expert WebShop performance.

C2.justification: The explanations involving UI understanding and shared interface elements are unchanged. Section 6 and Appendix B.3 retain the same limitations concerning successful-trajectory coverage, contextualization latency, and failure to generalize to unfamiliar UI elements.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same model choices, hyperparameters, training epochs, and demonstration counts; Appendix C retains identical prompts. The temperature-zero reproducibility statement and project/code-access information also match.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including comparisons with web-agent summarization approaches and automated prompting. The bibliography is repaginated without adding or removing works.

P1.justification: v2 adds an explicit equal-contribution footnote for Dongjun Lee and Juyong Lee and updates the version/date stamp. The scientific prose, terminology, section sequence, and appendix organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Spacing and figure/table placement change: Figure 5 moves from page 6 to page 7, and Table 2 from page 7 to page 8. Appendix pagination also shifts, while figure designs, captions, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies equal-contribution attribution and adjusts layout, but preserves the same method, results, interpretations, limitations, and reproducibility information throughout the main text and appendices. These limited editorial changes leave the paper's overall scientific quality and usability essentially unchanged.
